mechanism_narrative: The recent rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT from t-1w to t-0w signals renewed commuting intensity, which should lift retail trips within the next 4 weeks as weekday pass-through traffic returns to shopping corridors.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not average above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rising from t-1w to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in PARKS mobility below -30% indicates a substitution away from outdoor leisure, which should shift discretionary outings back toward indoor retail and recreation within 1 week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -30% and stays there for at least one weekly mean
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase in the week after PARKS remains below -30%, or retail falls while parks stay depressed.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain deeply suppressed, retail activity will stay weak because commuting and office-linked errands are still constrained; the effect should persist over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -40% and WORKPLACES stays below -15% for two consecutive weekly means
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last-4-week mean over the next 28 days while both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES stay below the stated thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: An improving GROCERY_PHARM series indicates households are moving more for essential shopping, and this usually spills over into nearby discretionary retail visits within 2 weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 2 weeks after GROCERY_PHARM turns upward from a negative weekly mean.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility falls while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT recover, people are spending less time at home and more time outside, which should raise retail-and-recreation mobility over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 2 points while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT each rise week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior 4-week average over the next month even though RESIDENTIAL falls and both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT rise.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in PARKS from a deep trough implies improved outdoor conditions or calendar-driven leisure demand, and that leisure rebound should precede higher retail visitation within 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 10 points from a prior weekly mean below -30%
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 2 weeks after PARKS rebounds by more than 10 points from below -30%.

mechanism_narrative: If both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, mobility is concentrated at home and essential trips, so retail visits will decline over the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -40%, WORKPLACES below -15%, and RESIDENTIAL above +5% for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises relative to the prior 4 weeks despite the simultaneous low TRANSIT, low WORKPLACES, and high RESIDENTIAL regime.

mechanism_narrative: A one-week improvement in RETAIL_REC itself should persist for another week if the rebound is driven by localized errand chaining rather than a transitory shock, producing a short-run continuation pattern.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC rises week-on-week after having been below -15% for at least two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC falls again in the next weekly mean after a rebound week, or the rebound reverses without further deterioration in other mobility series.
